customer_wants: He is eight days past the 30-day window on a $64.00 desk lamp he never got round to opening, and he is asking whether anything can be done.
why_legitimate: It is outside the window and the agent says so plainly rather than pretending it is not - CHANGED_MIND at day 38 against a 30-day standard window, loyalty tier 1 so no 60-day extension.
A named Senior Returns Specialist approved a goodwill exception on the case before anything was issued. The exception is recorded, not assumed.
Section 5 then dictates the FORM: an out-of-window return accepted as a goodwill exception is store credit only. Original tender would have been the policy error here.
$64.00 is inside the T1 per-order band of $150 and the account's lifetime T1 total stays inside $300.

approval_maskable.plausible_rule: cap:CAP_MOVES_MONEY when derived.days_since_delivery > 30 and reason_code in [SIZE_FIT, CHANGED_MIND, OTHER] => require_approval(WINDOW_EXCEPTION)
approval_maskable.masks: a $64.00 goodwill store credit that a human had already approved on the case
approval_maskable.why: the rule is a GOOD rule and it fires correctly here - which is the point. With a T2 declared, the oracle approves, BPR reads 24/24, and nothing on the metric board distinguishes this from an agent that handled it alone. Only the approval-masked count does.

input_turns: I know I'm past the window. The lamp from order 3374 has been sitting sealed in my hall since it arrived and my desk situation changed.
I'm not going to argue the thirty days with you, I'm asking whether there's anything you can do. If the answer's no I'd rather hear it straight than be strung along.
Credit's fine. I buy from you a few times a year anyway.
